title: Canada Has Not Shut Its Doors to Indian Students, Envoy Says
excerpt: Canadian High Commissioner Chris Cooter says the country has not reached its 2026 study permit cap and calls it the best time ever for Indian students to apply.
body:
• Canadian High Commissioner Chris Cooter said Canada has not reached its 2026 study permit cap of 408,000, calling it "probably the best time ever to apply" for Indian students.
  • Study permits issued to Indian students fell by half in 2025, but India remains Canada's top source country for international students.
  • Master's and PhD students at public Canadian universities are now exempt from the cap and no longer need a Provincial Attestation Letter.
  • Canada currently hosts 400,000 international students — more than the EU, UK, and Australia combined.

Canadian High Commissioner to India Chris Cooter pushed back against a growing perception that Canada has closed its doors to Indian students, telling ANI on June 22 that the country has room in its study permit cap and is actively seeking Indian applicants.

"There is a kind of misperception in India that Canada is shutting the doors. That is not at all the case," Cooter said in the interview. "We haven't even reached those caps. So actually, this is probably the best time ever to apply as an Indian student, because we want you there and there's space in these caps."

What Drove the Perception Shift

Canada introduced a cap on international students two years ago in response to a housing crunch and concerns about the quality of some educational institutions. The government cracked down on what Cooter described as "fly-by-night colleges," tightening regulations that had previously allowed unchecked growth in international enrollment.

The combination of the cap, the institutional cleanup, and a broader diplomatic rift between Ottawa and New Delhi sent a chilling signal to Indian families. Study permits issued to Indian students dropped by roughly 50 percent in 2025, according to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) data reported by Collegedunia.

""That's more than the EU, UK, and Australia combined."

"We haven't even reached those caps. So actually, this is probably the best time ever to apply as an Indian student, because we want you there and there's space in these caps."

— Chris Cooter, Canadian High Commissioner to India

The Numbers Behind the Cap

For 2026, IRCC set a target of up to 408,000 study permits — down from 437,000 in 2025 and 485,000 in 2024. That total splits into 155,000 permits for new arrivals and 253,000 for renewals. Cooter confirmed the cap has not been reached, meaning seats remain available.

One significant policy change benefits higher-degree applicants: master's and PhD students at public universities are now exempt from the cap. Since January 2026, they also no longer require a Provincial Attestation Letter, removing an administrative hurdle that had slowed applications.

Canada currently hosts approximately 400,000 international students. "That's more than the EU, UK, and Australia combined. It's more than the US hosts," Cooter said, highlighting the country's continued standing as a top destination for higher education.

What Indian Students Need to Know

For undergraduate and diploma applicants, the Provincial Attestation Letter requirement still applies, and applications count against the national cap. Students must show proof of funds, including a Guaranteed Investment Certificate of CAD 22,895 — approximately ₹15.2 lakh at current exchange rates — on top of first-year tuition fees. IRCC raised this amount in September 2025 for all 2026 applicants.

Cooter also pointed to the global standing of Canadian universities, noting that "many of our universities, for example, are in the top 100 — McGill, University of Toronto in the top 20 or so." He urged families to consider both universities and polytechnics, which Canada calls colleges, for high-quality education.

Diplomatic Thaw and Faster Processing

The envoy's remarks came against the backdrop of warming bilateral relations. He pointed to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's visit to India from February 27 to March 2, 2026, as a sign of the diplomatic thaw. Cooter also promised improvements in visa processing. "We're actively at work on fixing those problems," he said. "I'd like to see us be best in class."

What's Next

For Indian students and their families, the message is straightforward: fewer applicants in the current cycle mean reduced competition and better odds for those who apply to genuine institutions. The January 2027 winter intake is the next entry point, followed by the larger September 2027 fall intake. Students should apply early, secure funding, and choose only Designated Learning Institutions that lead to post-graduation work permits. The window is open, but it will not stay this wide indefinitely.
